narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Rain and thunderstorms are expected this evening into tonight as overcast conditions settle over the basin. Thunderstorms are possible this evening, peaking around 19:00. Warming through Sunday, with rain becoming more likely.

## Today's Forecast
Rain and thunderstorms are expected this evening into tonight, with the main onset window between 18:00 and 21:00 (85% probability). Total rainfall is expected around 5.5 mm (0.22 in). Overnight temperatures will drop to a low near 18.5°C / 65°F (following a daytime high of 28.5°C / 83°F). Peak gusts on land may reach up to 41.2 km/h (22 kt). Air quality remains Moderate across the urban area, with ground stations reporting an AQI range of 54 to 63, highest at Kisumu Airport (63 AQI). UV index exposure has ended for the day following dusk.

## Extended Outlook
Dry conditions develop heading into the weekend. By Sunday (Day 3), rain chances drop to 10% under warming temperatures up to 32.6°C / 91°F. Highs remain elevated into early next week before cloud cover and moisture return across the basin; by Thursday (Day 7), rain probability rises back to 30% with daily totals near 1.2 mm (0.05 in).

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Convective instability is elevated tonight, with model CAPE values reaching between 1020 J/kg (ICON) and 3570 J/kg (UKMO). Strong, sudden gusts and severe downdrafts are possible with any thunderstorm that develops this evening, regardless of the baseline surface wind forecast. Lightning and localized heavy downpours present the primary hazards through midnight.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters
Convective shower activity over the water will increase during dusk and the early evening hours. Peak wind gusts over Winam Gulf are forecast near 34.0 km/h (18 kt). Boaters and fishermen should exercise extreme caution, as nocturnal thunderstorms over the lake can produce sudden, dangerous wind shifts and localized rough waves far exceeding background wind speeds.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1008 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1019 hPa) — an 11 hPa spread, a strong large-scale gradient. Pressure is also falling toward the southwest, west — a large-scale feature building in that direction, though this sampling cannot say how fast or whether it will reach here. Pressure overhead is near-steady at 1015.0 hPa. Across the Nyanza Basin, mean sea-level pressure averages 1015 hPa today before trending downward slightly toward 1013 hPa over the next 24 to 48 hours, maintaining an environment favorable for evening trade-wind convergence and convection.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
The guidance behind this forecast is at least 9.0 hours old, as models were last aligned on the 06:00Z cycle. Model weighting for today's rain probability leans heavily on best_match and ECMWF IFS, as best_match is established at Day+0 as the strongest rainfall caller in the record. GFS and UKMO both show a strong tendency to under-forecast peak surface winds, so peak gust calls have been calibrated upward accordingly. The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) forecast for Kisumu calls for partly cloudy conditions tonight and sunny intervals on Friday (high of 28.0°C / 82°F, low of 20.0°C / 68°F), while noting rainfall in the wider regional outlook including Kisumu.

earlier_issuances.narrative_markdown:
## Overview
Slightly cooler and cloudier than yesterday. Dry until evening thunderstorms. Warming through Sunday, with rain becoming more likely.

## Today's Forecast
Temperatures reaching a daytime high of 28.5°C / 83°F before dropping to an overnight low of 18.2°C / 65°F. Conditions remain mostly dry through the morning and afternoon under extensive cloud cover. Evening thunderstorms are expected between 17:00 and 20:00, bringing an estimated 3.5 mm (0.14 in) of rainfall with an 85% probability of precipitation. Calibrated peak surface gusts on land will reach 40.8 km/h (22 kt); guidance does not share a unified compass bearing. Solar UV exposure reaches a maximum index of 9.0 (Very High) near midday. Air quality ranges from AQI 100 to 122 (Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups), with the highest reading recorded at Kisumu Airport.

## Extended Outlook
A warming trend develops over the next three days through Sunday (2026-09-20), with daytime highs rising to 31.4°C / 89°F to 32.0°C / 90°F and precipitation likelihood dropping to 15%. From Monday (2026-09-21) through Thursday (2026-09-24), confidence decreases as rain chances return; showers are expected to redevelop around Monday and Thursday (2026-09-24) with a 50% probability and daily precipitation totals around 0.8 mm to 2.2 mm (0.03 to 0.09 in).

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential
Convective instability is elevated this evening, with peak CAPE projected around 19:00. Model guidance displays significant divergence regarding instability levels: UKMO forecasts extreme CAPE up to 3330 J/kg and ECMWF builds to 1450 J/kg, while GFS and ICON keep peak CAPE lower around 640–670 J/kg. Strong, sudden downburst wind gusts far exceeding the 40.8 km/h (22 kt) background forecast are possible near any developing thunderstorm, regardless of light ambient surface winds.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters
Over the open waters of Winam Gulf, peak background wind gusts are forecast at 31.0 km/h (17 kt). Thunderstorms and showers are expected to move across the gulf between 17:00 and 23:00. Extremely high convective instability (UKMO CAPE 3000–3800 J/kg, ECMWF CAPE up to 1450 J/kg) over the lake supports localized severe downdrafts. Boaters and fishermen should prepare for sudden violent wind gusts and choppy waters during the evening and overnight hours.

## Detailed Discussion
### Synoptic Overview
Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the northeast (1008 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1019 hPa) — an 11 hPa spread, a strong large-scale gradient. The lower pressure to the northeast is filling over the next three days, while pressure is falling toward the west and southwest. Across the Nyanza Basin, mean sea-level pressure averages 1014–1016 hPa today before gradually weakening toward 1011–1013 hPa by Sunday and Monday.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes
Model consensus is weighted heavily toward ECMWF and ICON for short-term precipitation detection due to their strong Day+0 verification track records, while Best Match serves as the primary benchmark as the established top rain caller at Day+0. The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) local bulletin forecasts a high of 28.0°C / 82°F, a low of 20.0°C / 68°F, and afternoon/evening light showers, showing close agreement with the numerical consensus. Model guidance is at least 9.0 hours old (last aligned at 18:00Z on 2026-09-16), widening uncertainty for convective timing. Ground air quality monitoring stations report current AQI values as follows: Kisumu Airport at 122 (Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, PM2.5 122.0 µg/m³), Ochieng' Avenue in Kisumu Central at 101 (Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups, PM2.5 101.0 µg/m³), and Dunga Beach at 100 (Moderate, PM2.5 100.0 µg/m³).
